purpose: Build a modular, production-intended chatbot chatbot engine as a standalone API service. The engine relies on internally-coded memory, personality/soul, and state so that the typical weaknesses and inter-model differences of the underlying LLM are minimized. No orchestration framework owns the core: there is no LangGraph, Letta, or Zep acting as the brain. The turn loop, memory consolidation, context compilation, and identity continuity are all first-party code. Backends are reached through a single OpenAI-compatible Provider interface (covering OpenRouter, local vLLM, and Vast.ai-stood-up instances) plus a Modal ephemeral wrapper for episodic compute. Vectors live in Postgres via pgvector behind a VectorStore interface so a Qdrant swap later touches one adapter. Stack: Python 3.12, FastAPI, Postgres, Redis, Alembic, Docker Compose, uv. Everything is structured so voice, frontend, and visual modules attach later without touching the core.
async_strategy: Phases are dependency-ordered and act as synchronous boundaries; the supervisor advances a phase only when all its tasks are accepted. Within a phase, tasks are shaped for safe concurrency: interfaces/base contracts land in wave 1, concrete adapters and endpoints that depend only on those contracts run in parallel in wave 2 on disjoint allowed_write_paths, and fan-in wiring/tests run in a final wave via dependencies. Phase a (foundation) and the schema in phase c gate everything. Phases d (memory core) and e (soul/state) can overlap once phase c lands because they write disjoint paths. Phase g (the turn spine) fans in from b, d, and e.
cost_estimate: balanced. Bounded mechanical tasks (scaffolding, adapters, migrations, endpoint wiring, tests) route to cheap_first profiles with narrow allowed_write_paths and explicit acceptance_criteria. The two differentiating subsystems — the context compiler in phase d and the identity/persona logic in phase e — route strong_ok because their quality drives the whole product.
operator_questions: Embedding provider and dimension for v1 (local bge/e5 via the OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a hosted embedding) — fixes the pgvector column dimension in the 0001 migration.
Does the soul/state live entirely in Postgres (recommended for single-sourced state), or do you want a file-backed persona layer as well?
Single-tenant or multi-tenant schema for v1? It changes whether user_id is a hard partition key everywhere now or added later.
Modal usage pattern: on-demand per-request cold start, or warm-pool keep-alive windows — affects the ephemeral wrapper's lifecycle.
Streaming transport for /chat: SSE or WebSocket for v1?

phases.goal: Repository foundation and runnable infrastructure. uv-managed Python 3.12 project, Docker Compose bringing up Postgres+pgvector and Redis, typed config loader, Alembic initialized, and a FastAPI app skeleton exposing a health endpoint that everything else builds on.
phases.async_notes: Bootstrap is mostly sequential: pyproject + project package first (wave 1). docker-compose.yml, .env.example, and config.py can run in parallel in wave 2 on disjoint files. The FastAPI app skeleton + health endpoint and the Alembic init form wave 3 and depend on config.
phases.risk_notes: Foundation phase; every later phase depends on it. Keep dependencies minimal and approved-only. No business logic here.

phases.goal: Backend provider abstraction. A single Provider interface, an OpenAI-compatible adapter that serves OpenRouter, local vLLM, and Vast.ai-stood-up instances (base_url + key differ, contract identical), a Modal ephemeral wrapper handling cold-start/teardown, and a policy router that picks a provider per request. No first-party orchestration framework.
phases.async_notes: base.py (the Provider interface) is wave 1. openai_compat.py, modal_ephemeral.py, and router.py run in parallel in wave 2 on disjoint files, each depending only on base.py. tests/test_providers.py is the wave-3 fan-in.
phases.risk_notes: Provider interface is a public contract consumed by phase g. Lock its shape early; changing it later ripples. Validate any concrete OpenRouter model strings before execution per the backend/model rules.

phases.goal: Persistence and memory schema. SQLAlchemy models and the 0001 migration for users, sessions, messages, episodes, semantic facts, and entities; the pgvector embedding column; a VectorStore interface with a pgvector adapter; and an EmbeddingProvider interface. This is the single source of truth for state.
phases.async_notes: models.py + session.py land first (wave 1), the 0001 migration depends on models (wave 2). vector_store.py (interface) and embeddings.py (interface) run in parallel in wave 1; pgvector_store.py depends on vector_store.py + models. tests are the fan-in.
phases.risk_notes: Schema is foundational. Migration must be reversible. Embedding dimension must match the chosen embedding provider (see operator questions) or the pgvector column is wrong.

phases.goal: Memory core — the first differentiator. Working-memory buffer, episodic store, retrieval over the VectorStore with relational filtering, and the context compiler that assembles bounded, ranked context for each turn (not naive top-k).
phases.async_notes: working_memory.py and episodic.py run in parallel (wave 1, disjoint). retrieval.py depends on the store + episodic (wave 2). context_compiler.py depends on retrieval (wave 3). tests fan in.
phases.risk_notes: The context compiler is a core differentiator; route it to a strong profile. Keep retrieval logic first-party and deterministic so behavior is reproducible.

phases.goal: Soul and state engine — the second differentiator. Personality configuration, a durable state model, identity-continuity logic that resists drift across long horizons, and deterministic persona-prompt assembly. Internally coded so the persona does not depend on the underlying model's defaults.
phases.async_notes: personality.py and state.py run in parallel (wave 1, disjoint). identity.py depends on state (wave 2). persona_prompt.py depends on personality + identity (wave 3). May overlap phase d entirely since write paths are disjoint, but phase ordering keeps them as separate verification boundaries.
phases.risk_notes: Identity continuity is where chatbots usually fail. Route identity.py and persona_prompt.py strong. Keep state single-sourced in Postgres unless the operator opts into a file-backed layer.

phases.goal: Background consolidation workers. Hierarchical summarization, contradiction resolution, and decay/pruning of stale memory, wired into an idempotent run-scoped worker. This is the autonomous-memory-evolution layer the off-the-shelf engines do not do well.
phases.async_notes: summarizer.py, contradiction.py, and decay.py run in parallel (wave 1, disjoint). worker.py is the fan-in that schedules them (wave 2). tests fan in last.
phases.risk_notes: Workers must be idempotent and safe to re-run. Consolidation writes to the same memory tables phase d reads — keep operations transactional to avoid corrupting retrieval.

phases.goal: Chat orchestration spine and API. A thin explicit turn pipeline (receive -> retrieve -> compile context -> call provider -> extract/persist memory -> respond) with a clean step interface, plus the /chat, /sessions, and streaming endpoints. No LangGraph; the pipeline is first-party and fully inspectable.
phases.async_notes: steps.py (step interface) + turn.py (pipeline) land first (wave 1). chat.py, sessions.py, and streaming.py run in parallel in wave 2 on disjoint files. test_chat_e2e.py is the wave-3 fan-in and the real end-to-end gate.
phases.risk_notes: This is the spine that fans in providers (b), memory (d), and soul (e). The risk is leaking framework abstractions in; keep the step interface minimal so branching/tools can be added later behind it.

phases.goal: Integration tests, seed/dev tooling, and operations docs. End-to-end test across a full conversation with memory persistence and consolidation, a seed script for local dev, and an operations guide.
phases.async_notes: All three run in parallel; disjoint files, no inter-dependencies.
phases.risk_notes: Low. Documentation and tooling only; no core changes.
